title: Bug: PDDF CPLDMUX driver can hit a double free if the CPLDMUX fails to be created
author: nate-nexthop
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

When creating a CPLDMUX device using PDDF, in the case that the driver could not be instantiated (for example due to the I2C device not being present in the system) the driver will free some allocated memory. However it then calls platform_device_put() on a structure which now has a dangling pointer to the memory just free'd. This will result in a kernel panic when the pointer is free'd for the second time:
```
free_data:
    /* Free the allocated memory for platform and channel data */
    cpldmux_platform_data = plat_dev->dev.platform_data; // <----- Grab the pointer from the plat_dev struct
    if (cpldmux_platform_data)
    {
        printk(KERN_ERR "%s: Unable to register a cpldmux device. Freeing the platform data\n", __FUNCTION__);
        kfree(cpldmux_platform_data); // <----- Free the data
    }

    /* Put the platform device structure */
    platform_device_put(plat_dev); // <----- put the plat_dev struct which contains the dangling pointer.
```

### Steps to Reproduce

Instantiate a CPLDMUX device without the necessary hardware being present in the device.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Actual behavior: Kernel panic due to double free
Expected behavior: Device is failed to be created but no kernel panic

linkedPullRequests.title: PDDF CPLDMUX: Fix double free in cleanup case
linkedPullRequests.author: nate-nexthop
linkedPullRequests.body:
If we free this chunk of memory but don't set it to NULL, platform_device_put will try to free it later and panic the kernel.

By setting it to NULL, the other code won't free it.

#### Why I did it

If we don't set this field to NULL, platform_dev_put() will free the dangling pointer which has already been free'd. This will result in a kernel panic.

Fixes #23682 

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:

#### How I did it

Set the pointer field in the struct to NULL after free'ing it.

#### How to verify it

Run on a system with missing CPLDMUX hardware and observe no kernel panic.
